standard_text: The cell cycle: interphase and mitosis; the phases of mitosis (prophase, metaphase, anaphase, telophase) and cytokinesis; the importance of mitosis for growth and repair; cancer as uncontrolled cell division. key_big: Mitosis makes two identical daughter cells.
body_html:
How to think about it

The cell cycle has interphase (the cell grows and copies its DNA) and mitosis. In prophase chromosomes become visible; in metaphase they line up across the equator; in anaphase the chromatids are pulled to the poles; in telophase new nuclei form. Cytokinesis divides the cytoplasm.

Mitosis produces two daughter cells with the same number of chromosomes as the parent cell. It is needed for growth, repair of damaged tissue and asexual reproduction. Cancer happens when cells divide without control and form a tumour.

Example

In which phase do chromosomes line up in the middle?

Meta = middle

Answer: metaphase

Example

A human cell has 46 chromosomes. How many after mitosis?

Daughter cells are identical.

Answer: 46

Common mistakes

  • Thinking DNA is copied during mitosis.
  • Mixing up anaphase and telophase.
  • Thinking mitosis halves the chromosome number.
